calls.head: The Sabres should drive the play
calls.body: The Sabres have been around the middle of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Sabres to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Buffalo couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Buffalo usually gets better looks than most teams. Not tonight: a 4.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.6% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: The Blackhawks end a six-game winless run
paras: The Blackhawks won for the first time in seven games, after going 0-5-1. Owen Power got the scoring started for the Sabres midway through the first, but Frank Nazar tied it up for Chicago on the power play less than four minutes later. Tage Thompson restored the Sabres’ lead on the power play less than four minutes later. Nazar struck again midway through the third to tie it 2-2. Ryan Donato won it in overtime.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Spencer Knight settled in after a shaky start for the Blackhawks: he gave up two goals on the first six shots, then stopped the last 17, and Alex Lyon stopped 22 of 25 at the other end. The Hawks improved to 5-13-1, still last in the Central, while the Sabres fell to 8-7-4, sixth in the Atlantic.
